source_evidence.quote: ## B. Counterchanged tinctures: one reference acts differently by region

source.work: The Boke of Saint Albans, heraldic section
source.witness: 1486 text reproduced in the Blades facsimile edition, Project Gutenberg 71266
source.date: 1486: later than 1450; no earlier wording attestation claimed
source.ownership: Two complete adjacent chevron items on page 195: expository lead-in and figure call, Latin/French/English blazons, and both shields. Words read through the public-domain digital primary-text reproduction; shield images viewed natively. The full printed page was not separately collated.

complete_armorial_contents.latin: Portat arma quarteriata de nigro & argento cum vno signo capitali de dictis coloribus transmutatis.
complete_armorial_contents.image_check: Black/white quarterly field and chevron segments exchange values across its field division.

complete_armorial_contents.latin: Portat arma partita secundum longum de coloribus aureo & rubeo cum vno signo capitali de dictis coloribus transmutatis.
complete_armorial_contents.image_check: Vertical partition and opposed chevron regions observed. Monochrome image does not independently confirm gold/red; those are source-written colors.

design.attested_shared_reference: de dictis coloribus transmutatis refers back to the declared field pair; the same construction produces a different color on different portions of one charge according to field region.

productions: ArmorialContent := Field(Partition, ColorPair) Charge(Chevron) Counterchange(Charge, ThatField)
Counterchange := each charge portion has the opposite member of ThatField's ColorPair from its underlying region
provisional_semantic_contract.binding: Exactly one declared field and one shared color pair per example. Each region inherits that same field; no separately chosen color key per charge segment.
constraints: The partition determines which charge portions share underlying field color.
The same two-color pair governs every portion.
Charge and its underlying field differ in each region.
provisional_semantic_contract.projection: The formal object represents the armorial assertion. It does not silently claim to encode the whole trilingual expository paragraph; a whole-prose model must also account for its instruction, illustration call and language labels.

design.multistep_consequence: First bind the field partition and pair; then bind the chevron to that same field; the backward counterchange reference determines all regional charge colors jointly. A single uniform charge color cannot satisfy both regions, and copying the underlying field color erases the required contrast.

distinct_rivals.rule: Counterchanged is an independent uniform color label.
distinct_rivals.failure: A uniform charge color fails against one member of the declared field pair.

distinct_rivals.rule: The charge repeats the underlying field color.
distinct_rivals.failure: The source-image contrast is reversed or erased.

distinct_rivals.rule: Every charge segment gets a freely chosen color.
distinct_rivals.failure: It can imitate the picture but discards the shared two-color and reference constraints.

symmetries_and_risks: Simultaneous global color renaming preserves the relative rule; the relation alone cannot identify sable, silver, gold or red.
The examples change both partition and palette; they are not a controlled single-feature contrast.
The legible witness is later than the manuscript date range of interest; older Laud Misc.733 images requested for comparison timed out and remain unassessed.
A generic flexible heraldic description could fit almost any figure. Only the explicitly bounded shared-reference construction provides a restriction.
No admitted target paragraph or independently owned target field/charge relation is nominated; the source does not itself authorize a Voynich test.
